summary: The H27 README/script correction and sensitivity calculation are supported, and the sampled non-H27 artifact linkage matches. One additional source-audit qualification is required: the returned tree entries do not reproduce their reported root Git tree identifier. This is an evidence-integrity issue, not a counterexample to H27 or the proposed bound.
required_revisions: Document and reconcile the H27 root-tree commitment discrepancy in the source-audit addendum/manifest. Standard Git serialization of the seven returned root entries hashes to 0a3e3838650fc981133940e798c9d220140e785e, not the reported d4d5723267c662291efdadfa6e7061d919e76fa9. Until resolved, describe provenance-path absence as an observation about the returned listing rather than a cryptographically verified complete tracked tree, and preserve the mismatch without altering the original response.

findings.statement: The saved recursive tree response has117 entries and truncated=false, but its seven immediate root entries reconstruct Git tree0a3e3838650fc981133940e798c9d220140e785e instead of its declared d4d5723267c662291efdadfa6e7061d919e76fa9. A fresh nonrecursive connector fetch returned the same seven entries and declared identifier.
findings.disposition: Qualify the complete-tree claim or resolve the discrepancy. Both text blobs reproduce their identifiers and all18 represented non-root trees reconstruct correctly, so the issue is specifically the root commitment. No conclusion about the underlying mathematical theorem or hidden archive contents follows.

The addendum accurately states this sensitivity rather than claiming robustness to an unverified replacement.
